chunks: 1284 - What Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the salat in Makkah and al-Madīnah: should it be shortened or completed? He said: “Shorten, so long as you have not resolved to stay for ten days.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat being discussed in the context of travel
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, one of the two sacred cities mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: ten days, the duration that determines completing the prayer
key_terms.مُقَامِ: residing or staying in a place
key_terms.وَالْمَدِينَةِ: and al-Madīnah, the other sacred city mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.يُتَمُّ: is completed in full, as opposed to shortened
key_terms.يُقَصَّرُ: is shortened, referring to the travel form of salat

ai.seo_question: Should a traveler shorten or complete the salat in Makkah and Madinah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the salat of a traveler in Makkah and al-Madīnah. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that the prayer remains shortened unless one intends to reside for ten days, which establishes the criterion for completing the prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1284 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Imam al-Ridha (as) that He said:

I asked him about the prayer in Mecca and Medina, whether it should be shortened or completed.
Imam (as) said: "Shorten it unless you intend to stay for ten days”.
